title: Squares and long hexagons of a floor in Maku
subtitle: Floor tiling, Maku, Iran

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s SHAF27 drawing, its corners snapped to exact values. We devised the construction. Every corner comes from the point where the 45° line crosses the circle through A. The drawing gives no steps.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. The comparison with the drawing checks the finished lines, not how the design was first laid out. No photo of the floor was checked.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data199/SHAF27: Maku ‘armband’ floor tiling
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his drawing. He takes it from Javad Shafai, On decoration in Persian architecture and wood carving (Tehran, 1977), page 253: a floor tiling in Maku, Iran. The construction is ours.

given.O: The centre of a large sixteen-sided tile.
given.A: The middle of the next long hexagon.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through each of A and B. Draw a horizontal line through each of C and D. These lines make the square cell, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4. Draw a straight line through O and K1.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a horizontal line through C. They cross at K1, a corner of the cell. Draw a straight line through O and K1.

steps.text: The line through O and K1 crosses the circle at P. Draw a horizontal line through P. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The four lines make a square round O.

The horizontal line through P crosses the vertical line through A at M. The vertical line through P crosses the horizontal line through C at N. Draw a straight line through M and N. Draw a line through M at 90° to line MN.
Turn the two new lines through M round O by 90°, three times.
Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the lines picked out in orange. They make the small squares at the corners, the long hexagons between them and the large tile round O.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square tile side by side. A small square sits at every corner, with a long hexagon on each side of it.
